title: India Seals Fourth at Asian Games With 85 Medals After Late Gold Rush
excerpt: India finished fourth at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Saturday, winning 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals after a late two-day surge that delivered historic firsts in archery and golf.
body:
• India finished fourth at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games with 85 medals: 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze, after winning 11 of those golds in the final 48 hours.
  • Saturday's harvest included men's cricket gold over Pakistan, men's hockey gold over Malaysia with a direct ticket to the LA 2028 Olympics, and women's hockey gold — the first time India has swept both hockey titles at the Games.
  • Teenage archer Kumkum Mohod became the first Indian woman to win an individual recurve gold, and golfer Pranavi Urs won India's first women's individual golf gold; Aman Sehrawat upgraded his wrestling bronze to gold.
  • The final position could still shift slightly, with a couple of equestrian events on Sunday and India's nearest rival Uzbekistan still in contention.

Late Surge Salvages the Campaign

The star-studded cricket and hockey teams defended their crowns as expected, but it was a teenage archer and a debutant golfer who scripted the unexpected history that powered India to a creditable fourth place at the Asian Games in Nagoya on Saturday.

India could not repeat the 106 medals of the previous edition in Hangzhou, yet the final haul of 85 represents a decent return — one forged almost entirely in a frantic 48-hour finish. As of Thursday, India sat outside the top 10 with just 10 gold medals. Eleven golds across the last two days changed the complexion of the entire campaign.

In the end, India secured 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals. China (341), Japan (269) and South Korea (150) took the top three places, with India holding fourth ahead of Uzbekistan on 70.

Expected Golds in Cricket and Hockey

Abhishek Sharma was the familiar nemesis upfront, while Tilak Varma turned tormentor towards the end as India defended the Asian Games men's cricket gold with a 19-run win over Pakistan in Nisshin.

Shreyas Iyer's side posted 211 for 6 after Abhishek smashed 61 off 28 balls, studded with seven sixes, and Tilak silenced his critics with an unbeaten 51 off 22. Pakistan, powered by an unheralded Hasan Nawaz's 96 off 51 balls, were stopped at 192 for 6. India extended its dominance over its arch-rivals to six straight wins in T20 contests since the start of the 2024 World Cup.

On the hockey field it was India all the way, as captain Harmanpreet Singh rose to the occasion with a brace in a 5-1 win over Malaysia in the Kakamigahara final. Jugraj Singh, Hardik Singh and Shilanand Lakra also scored, and Harmanpreet finished as the tournament's top scorer with 12 goals. The gold secured direct qualification for the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.

The men's title came a day after the women defeated higher-ranked defending champions China 1-0 in the final to clinch the title after 44 years — also booking an Olympic spot. It is the first time India has won both the men's and women's hockey golds at the same edition of the continental showpiece.

Archers and Golfers Write History

Kumkum Mohod became the first Indian woman archer to win an individual recurve gold, edging South Korea's Oh Yejin 6-5 in the final after dispatching high-quality opponents in the earlier rounds. The Maharashtra teenager will head home with two gold and a silver from a dream debut — and, crucially, an individual quota place for India at the Olympics.

Golfer Pranavi Urs achieved a parallel historic first: India's first women's individual gold in golf. Unable to sleep the previous night with nerves, the 23-year-old from Mysore held on to a slender one-stroke lead in the final round, recovering from a triple bogey on the third hole with three birdies to finish at 15-under 265. Her performance also fetched India the team silver alongside Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar.

Olympic bronze-medallist Aman Sehrawat picked up top honours in the men's 57kg wrestling final, beating North Korea's reigning world champion Chong Song Han 10-7 to upgrade his Hangzhou bronze. India's wrestling contingent signed off with six medals, its best return since the 2018 Jakarta Games.

Where It Fell Short — and What Comes Next

The shortfall against the Hangzhou tally of 106 was felt most in shooting and badminton, where better was expected. But the campaign also showed historic growth in non-traditional disciplines — golf, equestrian and compound archery all delivered.

A couple of equestrian competitions are scheduled for Sunday, with India's nearest competitor Uzbekistan in the fray, so the fourth-place finish is not yet mathematically locked. Regardless, the story of this Asian Games for India is the last 48 hours: five golds on Saturday alone, a double hockey triumph that books two Olympic berths, and teenagers from Maharashtra and Mysore announcing themselves on the continental stage.

Diaspora Angle

For the Indian community in Nagoya and across Japan, the closing days offered the Games' defining storyline — a national contingent that looked out of contention on Thursday evening and finished Saturday with the tricolour rising repeatedly. The direct Olympic qualifications in hockey and archery mean several of these medal moments will have sequels at LA 2028.
